newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 5.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Hughes Electronics, a unit of General Motors, is seeking bids for its defense and aerospace businesses, which together could command about $8 billion.
- Continental Airlines initiated talks to be acquired by Delta Air Lines to pre-empt any move by rival American Airlines to become the top U.S. carrier.
- Cable Giant Tele-Communications Inc is preparing a cost cutting plan to include laying off about 5 percent of its staff and cutting executive staff.
- Ford Motor is contemplating closing some plants in the U.S. and Canada.
- Ford posted a 2.2 percent drop in November light-vehicle sales.
- Consumers are emerging from their late summer funk and are spending more freely.
- Microsoft is taking steps to control what PC users see when they first turn on their computers.
- Henkel sweetened its Loctite offer to $61 a share.
- A Dow Chemical and Lilly venture acquired a controlling stake in Mycogen.
- The dollar is being driven higher by major overseas governments and central banks.
- Rupert Murdoch is planning an ambitious expansion in the music industry and has quietly named his son James to lead the drive.
- Credit unions' worries mounted as a federal judge refused to stay his injunction sharply curtailing their ability to recruit new members.
- Kodak signed an agreement with Price/Costco to be the only major brand on the stores' shelves.
- Bond prices slumped in late afternoon trading as investors focused on a mix of events and rumors to take profits from recent gains.
- As Wall Street's ardor cools for household-name stocks, investors are favoring technology stocks, especially smaller ones, that can deliver surprising earnings growth.
